x: Ramanuja, the 11th–12th century Vaishnava teacher, propounded Vishishtadvaita, or qualified non-dualism. Nirguna Bhakti belongs to Kabir and Wahdat-ul-Shuhud to Ahmad Sirhindi.
t: Link each philosophy to its teacher.

x: Tulsidas, the great Rama devotee, composed the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi in the 16th century. Kabir was a Nirguna saint, while Raskhan and Chaitanya were Krishna devotees.
t: Link the text to its Rama Bhakti poet.

x: Option B is incorrect: Raskhan was a Muslim poet devoted to Krishna, not Rama, and wrote Prem Vatika. Chaitanya, Dadu Dayal and Kabir are correctly described.
t: Check the deity linked with each saint.

x: Mirabai sang of Krishna, Raskhan wrote Prem Vatika, Dadu Dayal founded the Dadu Panth, and the Alvars were Tamil devotees of Vishnu, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Recall the work or sect of each saint.

x: Both are true: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu of Bengal spread Krishna Bhakti within Vaishnavism, and the Tamil Nayanars were devotees of Shiva.
t: Discriminate the Alvars and Nayanars by deity.

x: Muinuddin Chishti brought the Chishti order to India and settled at Ajmer, where his dargah stands. Fatehpur Sikri is linked to Salim Chishti, Daulatabad to Burhanuddin Gharib and Gulbarga to Gesu Daraz.
t: Link each Sufi saint to his centre.

x: Nasiruddin Mahmud was called Chirag-i-Delhi, Salim Chishti lived at Fatehpur Sikri, Burhanuddin Gharib settled at Daulatabad, and Shaikh Mohammad Hussaini (Gesu Daraz) at Gulbarga, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Link each Sufi saint to his centre.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Nasiruddin Mahmud
(b) Salim Chishti
(c) Burhanuddin Gharib
(d) Shaikh Mohammad Hussaini

List-II
i. Gulbarga
ii. Chirag-i-Delhi
iii. Fatehpur Sikri
iv. Daulatabad

x: Both are true and R explains A: Dara Shukoh joined the Qadiri order as a disciple of its saints Mian Mir and Mulla Shah Badakhshi, which is why he is associated with the Qadiriya.
t: Check whether R gives the reason for the order Dara Shukoh belonged to.
s:
Assertion (A): Dara Shukoh was associated with the Qadiri order.
Reason (R): Dara Shukoh was a disciple of Mian Mir and Mulla Shah Badakhshi, saints of the Qadiri silsilah.

x: Ahmad Sirhindi of the Naqshbandi order was called Mujaddid Alif Sani, the reviver of the second Islamic millennium. Chirag-i-Delhi was Nasiruddin Mahmud and Mehboob-i-Ilahi was Nizamuddin Auliya.
t: Link each title to its saint.

x: Guru Nanak (1469–1539) founded Sikhism and taught Ik Onkar, the oneness of God. Angad, Arjan Dev and Gobind Singh were his successors as the second, fifth and tenth Gurus.
t: Recall the first Sikh Guru.

x: Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth, Guru Tegh Bahadur was the ninth Guru and was martyred, Guru Gobind Singh created the Khalsa in 1699, and Guru Ram Das founded Amritsar, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the key work of each Guru.

x: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj (first called the Brahmo Sabha) in 1828. The Tattvabodhini Sabha was Debendranath Tagore's, the Arya Samaj Dayanand's and the Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda's.
t: Link each organisation to its founder.

x: Debendranath Tagore led the Tattvabodhini Sabha and the Brahmo movement, Dayanand founded the Arya Samaj, Ramakrishna taught the unity of religions, and Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.
t: Link each reformer to his organisation.

x: Both are true: Keshab Chandra Sen was a leading Brahmo Samaj figure who later formed the Brahmo Samaj of India, and Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 to spread Vedanta.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Three are correct: Ram Mohan Roy with the Brahmo Samaj, Dayanand with the Arya Samaj and Ramakrishna with the unity of religions. The fourth is wrong because the Tattvabodhini Sabha was Debendranath Tagore's, not Keshab Chandra Sen's.
t: Check each pair separately.

x: All four are correct: Nanak named Bhai Lehna (Guru Angad) his successor, Amar Das set up 22 Manjis, Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth in 1604, and Tegh Bahadur was the ninth Guru.
t: Check each statement separately.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Guru Angad was appointed successor by Guru Nanak.
II. Guru Amar Das organised 22 Manjis.
III. Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth.
IV. Guru Tegh Bahadur was the ninth Guru.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: All four are correct: Nizamuddin Auliya was Mehboob-i-Ilahi, Nasiruddin Mahmud was Chirag-i-Delhi, Salim Chishti of Fatehpur Sikri was Shaikh-ul-Hind, and Shahabuddin belonged to the Suhrawardi order.
t: Check each statement separately.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Nizamuddin Auliya was known as Mehboob-i-Ilahi.
II. Nasiruddin Mahmud was known as Chirag-i-Delhi.
III. Salim Chishti was associated with Fatehpur Sikri and was known as Shaikh-ul-Hind.
IV. Shahabuddin was associated with the Suhrawardiya order.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Kabir worshipped a formless God, which is Nirguna Bhakti, and rejected idols and rituals. Krishna Bhakti belongs to Chaitanya and Mirabai, and Rama Bhakti to Tulsidas.
t: Discriminate Nirguna from Saguna Bhakti.

x: Shahabuddin belonged to the Suhrawardi order, which Bahauddin Zakariya brought to Multan. The Chishti, Naqshbandi and Qadiri orders were led by other saints.
t: Link the saint to his Sufi order.

x: Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki was a Chishti saint and a disciple of Muinuddin Chishti, while Baba Farid, called Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar, has verses in the Guru Granth Sahib, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the Chishti line of succession.

x: Both are true: Baba Farid and his disciple Nizamuddin Auliya were both major saints of the Chishti order, in the line after Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki.
t: Recall the Chishti line of succession.

x: Muinuddin Chishti brought the Chishti silsilah to India and set it up at Ajmer. Shahabuddin Suhrawardi is linked to the Suhrawardi order, Sharfuddin Yahya Maneri to the Firdausi order and Bahauddin Naqshband to the Naqshbandi order.
t: Link each silsilah to its founder.
s: Who established the Chishti Sufi silsilah in India?

x: Abdul Qadir Jilani of Baghdad founded the Qadiri silsilah. Bahauddin Naqshband founded the Naqshbandi order, and Maneri belonged to the Firdausi order.
t: Link each silsilah to its founder.

x: Bahauddin Naqshband of Bukhara founded the Naqshbandi silsilah, which Khwaja Baqi Billah brought to India. Jilani founded the Qadiri order and Shahabuddin the Suhrawardi order.
t: Link each silsilah to its founder.

x: Guru Nanak chose his disciple Bhai Lehna as successor and renamed him Angad, the second Guru. Ram Das, Hargobind and Tegh Bahadur were the fourth, sixth and ninth Gurus.
t: Recall the original name of Guru Angad.

x: Guru Nanak founded Sikhism, Guru Angad standardised the Gurmukhi script, Guru Amar Das set up the 22 Manjis, and Guru Ram Das founded Amritsar, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Recall the contribution of each Guru.

x: Both are true: Akbar granted land at the site of Amritsar in Guru Ram Das's time, and Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth in 1604.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Guru Hargobind, the sixth Guru, militarised the Sikhs with the Akal Takht and the two swords Miri and Piri. Har Rai being the seventh Guru is unrelated.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Guru Har Rai was the seventh Guru, Har Krishan the eighth, Tegh Bahadur the ninth and Gobind Singh the tenth, giving the order D, B, A, C.
t: Arrange the Gurus by succession number.

x: Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth, Guru Hargobind began the military tradition, Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed by Aurangzeb in 1675, and Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the key event of each Guru.

x: All three are correct: Guru Nanak founded Sikhism, Guru Angad standardised Gurmukhi, and Guru Arjan Dev built the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) at Amritsar.
t: Check each statement separately.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. Guru Nanak Dev was the founder of Sikhism.
II. Guru Angad Dev started and standardised Gurmukhi.
III. Guru Arjan Dev built Harmandir Sahib.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth and last human Guru. Before his death in 1708 he declared the Guru Granth Sahib the eternal Guru.
t: Recall the tenth Sikh Guru.
